## Goal (user story)

As a developer of the competitive mode, I want the balancing AI's decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `MainStreetAiPlayer`) adapted to shared-street competitive semantics, so the opponent plays competently on a street it does not fully own.

## Context

The existing heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street:
- `scoreBusinessAction` / `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction` value `(income + synergy) * horizon - cost` with no ownership concept.
- `aiPlanningHorizon` measures distance to the win threshold via `computeScore`, which sums a single player's coins + reputation.
- `enumerateLegalActions` includes staff actions (`hire-staff`, `peek-incident-deck`) — competitive mode makes staff player-only.

Parent: Main Street competitive mode epic (CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30). Depends on per-owner income routing (sibling) so scoring can evaluate against the acting player's own resources.

## Scope

- Ownership-aware scoring: evaluate income, synergy, and horizon against the **AI's own** resources/businesses and its own win threshold (using the per-player state model from the competitive state sibling).
- Staff exclusion: competitive-mode action enumeration drops staff actions from the AI's option space.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved.

## Out of scope

- Opponent-aware *denial* reasoning (blocking the opponent's best slot, buying to deny) — intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- Endless continuation — deferred to a separate top-level issue.
- N-player Monte Carlo — covered by the Monte Carlo harness sibling; architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner) but the initial harness validates head-to-head (1 human vs 1 AI).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** `scoreAction` and the per-type scoring helpers evaluate placement/upgrade/event value using only the acting player's resources and owned businesses, with the planning horizon computed from the acting player's own score vs. their win threshold.
- [ ] **AC2:** Competitive-mode legal-action enumeration excludes `hire-staff` and staff-skill actions (peek), while the single-player enumeration is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC3:** Deterministic: same seed + same strategy produces identical action sequences; verified by a dedicated deterministic replay test.
- [ ] **AC4:** All existing single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, hint consistency, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive AI tests (ownership-aware scoring, staff exclusion, determinism).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 — Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street
- Depends on: competitive state model + income/event routing siblings (per-player resources/score needed for ownership-aware horizon)

# Add Investor staff members

## Problem statement

The staff family has no member that manipulates the **market row** itself: every ability so far buffs income, reputation, costs, incidents or hand capacity. The Investor introduces a market-shaping role — one **free market re-roll per turn** that is **biased toward the business type where the Investor is employed** — giving players a reason to invest coins in scouting favourable offers rather than accepting the first row they see. Moving the Investor to a different business costs an action point, so the ability is a deliberate positioning decision rather than a free upgrade.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — wants a market-manipulation tool that rewards placing an Investor next to the business type they are trying to grow.
- **Main Street player (mid-game)** — wants a coin-free way to dig for a missing synergy piece (e.g. a Food business while running a Food cluster).

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a free market re-roll each turn while an Investor is employed, so that I can look for a better offer without paying the escalating re-roll cost (MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ).
- As a Main Street player, I want the Investor's free re-roll to be 75% likely to surface cards relevant to the business it is employed at, so that placing it near my cluster meaningfully improves my odds.
- As a Main Street player, I want to move the Investor to a different business for one action point, so that I can retarget the bias at a cost.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Investor card exists in the catalog.** A new `staff-investor` row is added to `src/card-data.csv` (feature flag `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`, bias `0.75`, no hand slots, generalist `allowedBusinessTypes`), with a tier assignment, cost, ongoing cost and description consistent with the staff ladder and the ×100 coin scale; it flows into the general market via the existing tier-gated staff deck (`createStaffDeck`).
- **AC2 — One free re-roll per turn.** While at least one Investor is employed, the player may perform **one** coin-free, action-free market re-roll per week/turn (no coin deduction, no action spent); multiple Investors do not stack (still one per turn). The free re-roll is gated by a per-turn flag reset at `WeekStart` alongside `peekUsedThisTurn`/`favourUsedThisTurn`, and it **advances the per-turn escalation counter** (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`, `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`) so the next paid re-roll costs the escalated price. Once used, further re-rolls fall back to the normal paid path.
- **AC3 — Relevance bias.** On the Investor's free re-roll, each drawn slot has a **75% chance** to be drawn from the "relevant" pool for the business the Investor is employed at, falling back to the fully random pool when the relevant pool is exhausted; the remaining probability is entirely random. Relevance is defined as a shared synergy type (business/community-space `synergyTypes`; event `targetSynergy`/effect; staff `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap with the hosting business's synergy types) — the free `refillSingleRowMarket` path is parameterised so the normal `refreshMarket`/`cycleMarketCards` paths stay fully random.
- **AC4 — All staff relocation costs an action point.** Relocating a hired staff member from one business to another is exposed as a player action and consumes **1 action point** for **all** staff (the existing `placeStaffOnBusiness` placement is action-free today and must be action-gated when used as a relocation; the initial placement at hire time remains part of the hire action). The move respects `allowedBusinessTypes` and employment-slot capacity, is undoable, and is persisted.
- **AC5 — UI & tooltips.** The market re-roll button/tooltip and the Investor's staff tooltip/employed-staff summary surface (a) whether the free re-roll is still available this turn and (b) the 75% relevance bias; the button label/tooltip reflect the coin-free state when available and the escalated cost when not. Wording stays consistent with the `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` "Research" rename if that lands first.
- **AC6 — Undo, save/load and determinism.** The per-turn free-re-roll flag, the per-turn escalation counter it increments (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`), the Investor's location and any bias state participate in undo/redo (`snapshotAction`) and in `MainStreetStateSerialize` (serialize + migrate backfill + deserialize), so mid-turn reload preserves both availability and the escalated next price; the bias draw uses the seeded RNG (`state.rng`) so same-seed ⇒ same-game determinism holds.
- **AC7 — Tests.** Unit/integration tests cover: catalog + CSV contract; free re-roll is coin-free, once per turn, resets at `WeekStart` and advances the escalation counter; the 75% relevance bias (deterministic with a seeded RNG) and its random fallback; movement action cost + undo + save/load round-trip; and existing re-roll/discount/action-economy tests are updated for the new card and counts.
- **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, the Main Street rules docs (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `content-design-and-progression.md`, `card-catalog.md`) and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- **AC9 — Quality gate.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **New mechanic, not just data.** The relevance bias and the free re-roll are new engine behaviour; they must be additive and must not change existing behaviour when no Investor is employed.
- **Single source of truth for re-roll cost.** The free re-roll must not silently bypass `refreshMarketCost()`; the paid path and its escalation (`MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`) remain authoritative for non-free re-rolls, and the free re-roll must increment the same per-turn escalation counter.
- **Reuse the market composition model.** `refillSingleRowMarket` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`) enforces the ≥1-business row composition; the biased draw must preserve that invariant.
- **Placement/employment invariant.** `business.employedStaff` and `staff.employedAtSlot` are kept in sync by the existing placement helpers; the move action must route through them.
- **Art drift guard.** `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` requires every unique card name to map to dedicated art or a documented pending-art target, and forbids growing the art-less baseline (currently 79). The Investor therefore needs a dedicated 1024×1024 sprite **or** an explicit, producer-approved pending-art entry (see `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`).
- **Coin scale.** All coin values are ×100 (per the integer-economy migration); the Investor's cost/ongoing cost must follow the existing staff ladder (`MS-0MULWBSF9000Z64Z`).

## Existing state

- **No Investor exists** anywhere in the repo or worklog (searched `investor`, case-insensitive, excluding `node_modules`/`dist`); only the unrelated `Investor Bonanza` event fixture appears in a test.
- **Market re-roll is already action-free** (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §6.0 "Free operations: Market re-roll/refresh"), so "without using an action" means the Investor's re-roll is free of **coins** as well; the normal re-roll costs `REFRESH_MARKET_COST` (500, escalating per `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`).
- `refillSingleRowMarket(state)` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:162`) builds the row: 3 slots, ≥1 business, at most 1 upgrade / 1 event / 1 staff, drawing via `state.rng` (seeded).
- `refreshMarket(state)` / `refreshMarketCost(state)` / `canRefreshMarket(state)` live in `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`; discounts come from `refreshCostDiscount` staff and the Negotiator skill.
- **Staff placement is free today**: `placeStaffOnBusiness` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:880`) explicitly consumes no action/coins; `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand`/`removeStaffFromBusinessCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:674/692`) wrap it in `snapshotAction`. There is currently **no** player-facing "move staff" action.
- Staff card fields live in `StaffCard` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts:330`), parsed in `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` (CSV columns incl. `actionsPerTurn`, `peekOncePerTurn`, `allowedBusinessTypes`); the catalog currently holds **25** staff rows.
- Per-turn gates (`peekUsedThisTurn`, `favourUsedThisTurn`, `businessPlacedThisTurn`) are reset in `executeWeekStart` (`src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`).
- Card-count baselines that will shift when a staff row is added: `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` (`toHaveLength(25)`), `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` (166 / 174 totals), `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`, `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json`.

## Desired change

- **CSV/catalog:** add `staff-investor` with a new bias column (e.g. `marketRelevanceBias = 0.75`) plus a free-re-roll marker (e.g. `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`), no `handSlotsAdded`, generalist `allowedBusinessTypes`, and a description in the existing "reduces X by Y" house style.
- **Types/parsing:** add the new optional `StaffCard` fields and parse them in `MainStreetCardsTemplates` (numeric column for the bias; boolean/flag column for the ability).
- **Engine:** add `investorFreeRerollUsedThisTurn` state (reset at `WeekStart`), a `canUseFreeMarketReroll`/`useFreeMarketReroll` pair (coin-free, action-free, once per turn) that **increments `marketRefreshesThisTurn`**, and a `refillSingleRowMarket`-compatible biased draw parameterised by the hosting business's synergy types + `0.75`.
- **Movement:** add a move-staff engine function + command that charges 1 action via the existing weekly action budget for **any** staff relocation, reusing `placeStaffOnBusiness` semantics (adding the action gate at the command layer).
- **Serialization:** add the new state field to serialize, migrate (backfill `false`/`0`) and deserialize.
- **UI:** market re-roll button/tooltip shows the free re-roll availability; staff tooltip/employed-staff summary states the free re-roll + 75% bias; a move-staff affordance that costs an action.
- **Docs & art:** update the rules/catalog/progression docs; add the Investor sprite (or a documented pending-art entry) and regenerate `card-art-map.json`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `staff-investor` row (new bias column + free-re-roll flag; tier, cost, ongoing cost, description).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `StaffCard.freeMarketRerollPerTurn?` / `StaffCard.marketRelevanceBias?` (+ doc comments).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — parse the new CSV columns into the new fields.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — free re-roll path (`canUseFreeMarketReroll` / `useFreeMarketReroll`), bias-aware `refreshMarket` variant, and cost/label reporting.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — parameterise `refillSingleRowMarket` with an optional relevance pool; keep the default path unchanged.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — reset the per-turn free-re-roll flag.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — new per-turn state field (and serialized-state entry).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialize, migrate backfill (and deserialize) the new field.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` / `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — move-staff engine function + command (1 action), free-re-roll command.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` / `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — helpers to detect the employed Investor and its hosting business synergy types.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — free-re-roll button state, tooltip and availability text.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — employed-staff summary / staff tooltip line for the new ability.
- `src/card-art-map.json`, `src/sprites/`, `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` — Investor art (or a documented pending-art entry).
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — free re-roll, relevance bias, movement cost.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — staff table row + ability cell.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — staff catalogue row.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`, `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` — catalog baselines.
- `tests/main-street/` — new `investor-staff.test.ts` (free re-roll, bias, movement) plus updates to `refresh-market.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts`, `meta-progression.test.ts`, `staff-business-type-matching.test.ts`, `card-art.test.ts`, `hud-tooltips.test.ts`, `action-economy.test.ts` and any staff-count assertions.

## Related work

See **Related work (automated report)** below, plus manually identified items:

- `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` — "Reroll to cost more" (open): escalates the paid re-roll cost; its appendix explicitly leaves "free re-rolls do not advance the escalation counter" as an assumption to settle with this item.
- `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` — "Rename the reroll button 'Research'" (in-progress): touches the same market re-roll button/tooltip; coordinate wording and the free-re-roll affordance.
- `MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0` — "Some staff cards should add action points" (completed): establishes the weekly action budget and the staff card UI/action patterns the movement cost builds on.
- `MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M` — "Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects" (completed): most recent end-to-end staff-ability implementation (CSV → engine → docs → tests); follow its structure.
- `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` — "Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card" (open): owns the art-less baseline; the Investor raises the drift-guard question.
- `MS-0MUAYBAHW007RMSL` — "Add a charity shop" (completed): precedent for adding a card and updating the catalog/count baselines.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Decision (free = coins-free, escalation-advancing):** because market re-roll is already action-free, "free re-roll, without using an action" means **no coin cost and no action cost**, but the free re-roll **advances** the per-turn escalation counter. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (bias definition):** "relevant to the type of business they are currently located at" = shares a synergy type with the hosting business; businesses/community-space by `synergyTypes`, events by `targetSynergy`, staff by `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (bias application):** the 75% applies per drawn slot with a random fallback; the entire row is not a single 75% roll. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (no stacking):** multiple Investors still grant a single free re-roll per turn (avoids a degenerate multi-Investor loop). *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (movement scope):** **all** staff relocation costs an action; the initial placement at hire time is unchanged. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Risk (scope creep / existing behaviour):** the re-roll cost item and the rename item touch the same button; implementing the free re-roll without advancing the counter would desynchronise the displayed price, and newly action-gating **all** staff relocation changes an existing free operation (and its tests). Mitigation: keep `refreshMarketCost()` authoritative, increment the shared counter on the free re-roll, and update the staff-placement tests in the same change.
- **Risk (determinism/tests):** adding a card changes seeded deck draws and several fixed-count baselines; many fixtures inline counts. Mitigation: update the documented baselines and count assertions in the same change, and cover the bias with a seeded-RNG test.
- **Risk (art drift guard):** a new art-less card fails `card-art.test.ts`; either supply a sprite or get a producer-approved pending-art entry, otherwise the item is blocked by `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`.
- **Risk (save compat):** forgetting the migrate backfill leaves old saves with `undefined` and a throwing/NaN free-re-roll gate. Mitigation: backfill in `migrateSerializedState` and assert a round-trip.
- **Risk (balance):** a free re-roll per turn plus a 75% biased row is a strong information advantage; cost/tier may need balancing (`balancing-methodology.md`). Mitigation: pick a mid/premium tier and revisit after playtest.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Round 1 (route: herdr auto-dispatch, 2026-09-30; answered by the producer 2026-09-30).**

- **Q1 (free re-roll semantics):** "The market re-roll is already action-free, so what does the Investor's 'free re-roll' free you from, and does it stack/interact with the escalating cost (`MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`)? Options: (a) one **coin-free** re-roll per turn, does **not** advance the escalation counter, multiple Investors do **not** stack; (b) one coin-free re-roll per Investor (stacks); (c) the free re-roll also resets the escalation counter; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** one coin-free, action-free re-roll per turn; it **does advance the escalation counter**; multiple Investors do **not** stack.

- **Q2 (relevance definition & application):** "How is 'relevant to the type of business they are currently located at' defined, and how does the 75% apply? Options: (a) a shared synergy type (business/community-space `synergyTypes`, event `targetSynergy`, staff `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap), applied **per drawn slot** with random fallback; (b) relevant by exact business name only; (c) the **whole row** is 75% likely to be relevant; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** as recommended — **(a)** shared synergy type, applied per drawn slot, with random fallback.

- **Q3 (movement cost & scope):** "Staff placement is action-free today. Should the Investor's move cost an action point, and does that apply to all staff? Options: (a) **Investor only** pays 1 action to relocate; other staff stay free; (b) **all staff** relocation costs 1 action; (c) the move is free but limited to once per turn; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** **(b)** — **all** staff relocation costs 1 action.

**Secondary assumptions (not asked in Round 1, to keep to the ≤3-question limit):**

- **Card economics (default):** `staff-investor` is a generalist (all synergy types), `handSlotsAdded: 0`, tier 5, cost 1000, ongoing 125 — mirroring the tier-5 specialist band (Financial Advisor). *Recorded as an assumption; the producer may re-balance.*
- **Art (default):** add a dedicated 1024×1024 Investor sprite and regenerate `card-art-map.json`; if art cannot be produced, request a producer-approved pending-art entry so the drift guard passes.
- **Rename coordination (default):** implement the free-re-roll affordance on the existing re-roll button so it survives the `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` "Research" rename without conflicting wording.

**Research finding (agent, 2026-09-30):** The free re-roll and relevance bias are **not** implemented anywhere (repo + worklog search). The re-roll is already action-free and coin-costed (`src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`); `refillSingleRowMarket` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:162`) is the single composition point; staff placement is action-free (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:880`). This item is therefore a **new mechanic + card + docs + art** change, not a data-only change.

## Goal (user story)

As a player who just reached the win threshold in endless mode, I want an "Enter Endless Mode" button on the end-game dialog so I can continue playing beyond the threshold.

## Context

CG-0MTIILU5V006GCN4 wired the endless-mode logic: when `config.endlessMode === true` and a player reaches the score threshold, the engine sets `endReason = 'score_threshold_continue'` and keeps `gameResult = 'playing'`. The end-game dialog (`MainStreetOverlayContent.showGameOverOverlay`) already reads `endReason` for display, but the player has no way to actually continue — the only options are "Play Again" (restart) and "Menu" (quit). This leaves the endless-mode feature inert from a player-facing perspective.

## Scope

- Add an "Enter Endless Mode" button to the end-game dialog when `endReason === 'score_threshold_continue'`.
- When pressed, the button dismisses the overlay and resumes gameplay from the current state (no restart).
- The button is hidden in all other end-reasons (normal win, bankruptcy, turn exhaustion, etc.).

## Out of scope

- Competitive mode endless mode (separate CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 children).
- UI changes to the main menu or difficulty selector.
- Any Monte Carlo or AI changes.

# Reroll to cost more

## Problem Statement

Main Street's market re-roll currently costs a flat 500 coins (`REFRESH_MARKET_COST`), so a player can re-roll repeatedly within the same turn at the same price and brute-force a favourable market row. The cost should escalate with every re-roll made in the same turn (500, 750, 1000, and +250 each time) and reset at the start of each turn.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — "As a player, I want each successive market re-roll in a turn to cost 250 more than the last, so that re-rolling is a meaningful, escalating economic decision rather than a cheap reset of the market row."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Escalating cost:** Within a single turn, the first re-roll costs 500 coins, the second 750, the third 1000, and each subsequent re-roll costs 250 more than the previous one.
2. **AC2 — Turn reset:** The re-roll escalation resets to the 500 base at the start of each turn (the `WeekStart` day boundary, alongside the other per-turn gates).
3. **AC3 — Staff discounts preserved:** Existing refresh-cost discounts (Accountant `refreshCostDiscount`, Negotiator specialization skill) continue to be subtracted from the escalated base cost, clamped at 0 (never negative).
4. **AC4 — Legality & UI:** `canRefreshMarket()` and the re-roll button label/tooltip report the current escalated cost, and the button is disabled (with the existing "not enough coins" reason) when the player cannot afford it.
5. **AC5 — Undo & persistence:** The per-turn re-roll count participates in undo (a re-roll can be reversed) and in save/load serialization, so reloading mid-turn preserves the escalated price.
6. **AC6 — Tests:** Unit tests cover the 500/750/1000 progression, the per-turn reset, discount interaction, and undo/save-load round-trip; affected existing tests are updated.
7. **AC7 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **AC8 — Quality gate:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Only the escalation schedule is new; staff discount values are unchanged.
- The refresh cost must stay centralised in `refreshMarketCost()` so every call site (legality check, command, UI) sees the same escalated price.
- Free-reroll abilities are not yet implemented (see CG-0MTISBYLS009936W); they are out of scope for this item.

## Existing State

- `REFRESH_MARKET_COST = 500` in `src/MainStreetCardsConstants.ts` (re-exported via `MainStreetCards.ts`).
- `refreshMarketCost(state)` in `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` subtracts summed staff `refreshCostDiscount` plus the Negotiator skill discount and clamps at 0.
- `canRefreshMarket(state)` gates on `MarketPhase` and affordability; `refreshMarket(state)` deducts the cost, discards visible cards, refills the row, and logs.
- `refreshMarketCommand(state)` in `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` wraps the action in `snapshotAction` for undo/redo.
- There is currently **no** per-turn re-roll counter on `MainStreetState`.
- `executeWeekStart()` in `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` already resets the other per-turn gates (`peekUsedThisTurn`, `favourUsedThisTurn`, `businessPlacedThisTurn`).
- The re-roll UI label already renders `refreshMarketCost(s.state)` in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` lists fields explicitly in three places (serialize, migrate backfill, deserialize), so a new counter must be added to all three.
- `tests/main-street/refresh-market.test.ts` (AC2) currently asserts "unlimited per turn while affordable" at a flat cost — this assertion must change.

## Desired Change

- Add a `REFRESH_MARKET_COST_STEP` (working name) constant = 250 next to `REFRESH_MARKET_COST`.
- Add a `marketRefreshesThisTurn: number` field to `MainStreetState` (default 0), documented in `MainStreetStateTypes.ts`.
- `refreshMarketCost(state)` returns `Math.max(0, REFRESH_MARKET_COST + REFRESH_MARKET_COST_STEP * marketRefreshesThisTurn - discounts)`.
- `refreshMarket(state)` increments `marketRefreshesThisTurn` on a successful re-roll (so the reported/charged cost is the pre-increment value).
- `executeWeekStart()` resets `marketRefreshesThisTurn = 0`.
- Initialise the counter in `setupMainStreetGame`; serialise it, backfill it in `migrateSerializedState`, and restore it in the deserializer.
- Update the affected tests and the Main Street rules documentation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetCardsConstants.ts` — add the 250 escalation step constant alongside `REFRESH_MARKET_COST`.
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` — re-export the new constant if it follows the existing barrel pattern.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — add the `marketRefreshesThisTurn` state field (and serialized-state type entry).
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — `refreshMarketCost()` computes the escalated base; `refreshMarket()` increments the counter.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — reset the counter at `WeekStart`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — initialise the counter to 0.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialize, migrate (backfill 0), and deserialize the counter.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — verify the label/tooltip/disabled state use the escalated `refreshMarketCost()` (likely no code change; confirm).
- `tests/main-street/refresh-market.test.ts` — replace the flat "unlimited per turn" case with escalation + reset coverage.
- `tests/main-street/staff-skill-buff-wiring.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` — update discount assertions for the escalated/unchanged first-roll cost.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — document the escalating re-roll cost and per-turn reset.

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Assumption (discounts):** staff discounts keep applying to the escalated base, clamped at 0 — pending producer confirmation (see Appendix).
- **Assumption (free re-rolls):** a free re-roll does not advance the escalation counter — pending producer confirmation (see Appendix).
- **Assumption (unbounded):** escalation has a fixed 250 step and no upper bound; affordability is the practical cap — pending producer confirmation (see Appendix).
- **Risk (undo/redo):** if the counter is not part of the undo snapshot, undoing a re-roll would refund coins while leaving the higher next price, producing an inconsistent cost. Mitigation: rely on the existing whole-state snapshot and assert undo restores both coins and counter.
- **Risk (save/load):** forgetting the migrate backfill would make pre-existing saves load `undefined` and NaN the cost. Mitigation: backfill `?? 0` in `migrateSerializedState`.
- **Risk (existing tests):** the "unlimited per turn" assertion and flat-cost discount assertions will fail once escalation lands. Mitigation: update them in the same change.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the free-reroll and rename items touch the same area; they are deliberately excluded so this item stays a focused cost change.

## Related Work

- `CG-0MTKMN7KG006F5EE` — "The cost of a reroll is still 5, it should be 500" (completed, v0.1.17): set the flat base cost to 500; this item builds the escalation on top of it.
- `CG-0MTISBYLS009936W` — "Add Investor staff members" (open): a staff ability granting one free market re-roll per turn; interaction with the escalation counter must be settled (see assumptions).
- `CG-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` — "Rename the reroll button 'Research'" (open): touches the same UI label; coordinate if both land together.
- `CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4` — "Group F: Staff — abilities beyond hand slots (4 cards)" (completed): introduced the Accountant `refreshCostDiscount` applied by `refreshMarketCost()`.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions and Answers

- **Open Question:** Should existing staff refresh-cost discounts (Accountant `-1`, Negotiator skill) continue to apply to the escalated cost (e.g. 750 − 1 = 749), or does the progressive schedule replace discounts? — **Status: OPEN — producer confirmation requested.** Working assumption: discounts continue to apply to the escalated base and the result is clamped at 0.
- **Open Question:** Should a free re-roll (future Investor staff, `CG-0MTISBYLS009936W`) advance the escalation counter, i.e. make the next paid re-roll more expensive? — **Status: OPEN — producer confirmation requested.** Working assumption: no — a free re-roll neither charges coins nor advances the progression; to be reconciled when the Investor item is implemented.
- **Open Question:** Is the escalation unbounded ("and so on")? — **Status: OPEN — producer confirmation requested.** Working assumption: unbounded, with a fixed 250 step; affordability is the practical cap.

# Add images for all cards

## Problem Statement

The Main Street card redesign (CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN) reserves a 64×64 left-art graphic zone on every card face, but all 162 cards currently display only a placeholder (synergy-coloured rectangle with a single-letter initial). Images must be generated from the `art_notes` descriptions in `card-data.csv`, packaged as PNGs, and embedded into the SVG card rendering pipeline so they appear alongside the card text.

## Users

- **Players**: See distinctive, thematic imagery on every card face in their hand, on the street, and in the market — improving recognisability and atmosphere.
- **Developers**: Have a reproducible image-generation pipeline that produces one PNG per card from `art_notes`, with a safe fallback to a generic placeholder when no image exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every card across all families (business, community-space, event, upgrade, staff) has an associated 64×64 PNG image file in `public/assets/games/main-street/cards/`.
2. Images are named `<card_id>_64_x_64.png` (e.g. `biz-bakery_64_x_64.png`) and are referenced by the SVG card generator, which attempts to embed the corresponding PNG and falls back to a generic placeholder when the file is missing.
3. The `graphicZoneSvg()` function in `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` is updated to embed `<image>` elements for the PNG assets (with a fallback `<rect>` + glyph when the image is unavailable or fails to load).
4. All 162 card entries in `card-data.csv` have an `art_notes` value — cards that previously had none receive a generic placeholder description.
5. The full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Risks & Mitigations

- **Image generation quality**: AI-generated images may not match the intended aesthetic. Mitigation: producer reviews images before committing to the repo; a script to regenerate is preferred over manual editing.
- **SVG `<image>` fallback reliability**: SVG `<image>` elements do not gracefully handle missing files — the zone may render blank. Mitigation: the SVG generator emits the `<image>` element, and when the file is absent, falls back to the existing `<rect>` + glyph placeholder.
- **Licensing**: Generated images must be clearly documented as CC0 / self-authored. Mitigation: update `CREDITS.md` with provenance for every new asset directory.
- **Scope creep**: "Every card" could imply artwork for other example games (Golf, Lost Cities, etc.). Mitigation: scope is strictly Main Street 162 cards.

## Constraints

- Images must be permissive / freely available for commercial use (CC0, MIT, or self-authored).
- The naming convention must be deterministic from the card id so the SVG generator can derive asset keys at runtime without additional configuration.

# Problem statement

The contextual first-bank hint overlay (CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P) fires during the tutorial when the player ends a turn with spare actions, creating a "dead end" that interrupts tutorial progression and confuses the tutorial state machine. The hint is designed for normal gameplay and should not fire while the tutorial is active.

## Users

- **New players** completing the Main Street tutorial — they expect a linear, guided experience. An unexpected banking hint overlay mid-tutorial interrupts this flow, potentially showing a stale or completed tutorial step after the hint is dismissed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Banking hint does not fire during tutorial:** The contextual first-bank hint trigger in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` must check that `tutorialController.isActive` is `false` (i.e., the tutorial is not active). The hint must never fire while the tutorial overlay is showing or a tutorial step is pending.
2. **Banking hint fires in normal gameplay:** The hint continues to fire exactly once when a non-tutorial player ends a turn with `actionsRemaining > 0`, respecting the persistence flag (`hasSeenBankingHint`).
3. **No regression to tutorial flow:** Existing tutorial steps, overlay lifecycle, and step progression remain unchanged. The tutorial still completes through all 26 steps without interruption from the banking hint.
4. **No regression to banking hint:** The hint still triggers correctly in normal gameplay after the tutorial is complete (on the first end-turn with spare actions).
5. **All tests pass:** Existing tutorial unit and browser tests pass; no new failures introduced.

## Constraints

- **Minimal change:** Only the trigger condition in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` needs modification (one logical operator change). No new fields, no structural changes.
- **Tutorial-layer only:** The fix is entirely within Main Street's tutorial wiring; no core-engine, card-system, or UI component changes.
- **Existing banking hint implementation preserved:** The `BANKING_HINT_STEP`, `renderBankingHint()`, and `TutorialState` banking hint flag remain unchanged.

## Existing state

- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** implemented the contextual first-bank hint with the following trigger in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()`:
  ```ts
  if (tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0) {
      pendingBankingHint = true;
      // persist flag via TutorialState
  }
  ```
- This condition fires when the tutorial is **active** AND the player has spare actions.
- The `renderBankingHint()` method saves the current tutorial step, shows the banking hint overlay, and on dismiss tries to restore the saved step — but if the tutorial step has already advanced (e.g., T6 End Turn completed), the restoration shows a stale step, creating the "dead end."
- The intent from the original brief (CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P) was that the hint fires **once per save** on the first bankable end-turn — but the implementation does not distinguish between tutorial and normal gameplay contexts.

## Desired change

Change the trigger condition in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` from:
```ts
if (tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0)
```
to:
```ts
if (!tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0)
```

This ensures the banking hint only fires in normal gameplay (after the tutorial is complete), never during the tutorial.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — One-line fix: invert the `tut?.isActive` check in the banking hint trigger (endTurn path, ~line 221).

## Related work

- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** (completed, merged) — Main Street: tutorial coverage for action banking (parent feature that introduced the contextual first-bank hint).
- **CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR** (completed, merged) — Main Street: action banking (engine-level banking logic).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** If the producer believes the banking hint should also fire during the tutorial (e.g., as an optional teaching moment), that would require a different design — but the title and description indicate this is clearly unintended.
- **No edge cases:** The banking hint has a one-shot persistence flag; if the hint never fires during the tutorial (which is the fix), it will fire on the player's first non-tutorial end-turn with spare actions — this is the intended behaviour.

Main Street has no charity shop: a low-cost, Culture-synergy business that trades a modest income for a steady reputation trickle. The producer has specified the card's core economy (1.5 income/turn, 0.15 reputation/turn, cost 3 at the pre-scale convention), and this work adds the card to the pool so players gain an early reputation-leaning Culture business at tier 2.

## Users (example user stories)

- **As a player**, I can buy a Charity Shop for 300 coins and place it on the street, where it produces a small income and a steady reputation gain each turn, giving me an early Culture-synergy building with a reputation focus.
- **As a player**, I expect the Charity Shop to participate in Culture adjacency synergy like other Culture businesses (Bookshop, Craft Shop), so I can cluster it with my Culture cards.
- **As a maintainer**, I expect the new card to be a first-class registered template — present in the CSV, the tier/progression system, generated metadata and card art — with all template-count and consistency tests updated rather than special-cased.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Card data.** `src/card-data.csv` contains a new business row with exactly: `family = business`, `id = biz-charity-shop`, `name = Charity Shop`, `cost = 300`, `baseIncome = 150`, `synergyTypes = Culture`, `upgradePath` empty (standalone), `maxLevel = 0`, `reputationPerTurn = 15`, `ongoingCost = 75`, `tier = 2`, plus a non-empty `description` and `art_notes`. 2. **Registered template.** The card is loaded by `MainStreetCards.ts` as a business template, is available at tier 2 through the tier/`CARD_TIER_MAP` progression, and appears in the business deck built by `createBusinessDeck()`.
3. **Generated metadata and art.** `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` lists `biz-charity-shop` under `expandedCardIds.business`, and `node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` produces `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/biz-charity-shop.svg`; both are committed.

   - the hardcoded tier-2 synergy snapshot in `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` becomes `{ Commerce: 2, Service: 1, Culture: 1 }`.
   The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
5. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (business table, deck-size/expansion counts, synergy-type coverage) and any relevant README or docs-site entries. **Note:** `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Existing state

- `CG-0MUAYBA0L000XLK3` — Pawn shop should reduce, not increase reputation (sibling migrated producer note; establishes the ×100 value convention for business cards).

# Intake Brief: Main Street — Business Payback Rebalance (~5 Turns) and Economy Re-tune

**Work item:** MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3 · `task` · `high`

## Headline

Re-derive business `baseIncome` so a business pays for itself in **~5 turns on
average** (cheaper businesses faster, more expensive slower), then re-tune the
compensating balance levers, capture before/after Monte Carlo evidence, and
produce prioritised further-balancing recommendations.

## Problem statement

The cost/income balance makes the game too easy: a business currently recovers
its purchase cost in **~1.3–2.4 turns** (net of its per-turn running cost), so
buildings become profitable almost immediately and runs snowball. On the
canonical harness profile the greedy AI wins 91 % (Easy) / 61.5 % (Medium) /
44 % (Hard) with elevated net liquidity (~6.3 coins/turn on Medium). The
producer wants business payback slowed to a ~5-turn average — with a cost-graded
spread — and the surrounding economy re-tuned so the game stays challenging but
winnable, backed by simulation evidence and concrete follow-up suggestions.

## Users

- **Player** — wants building decisions to carry real economic tension (when to
  buy, which business, how many turns until it pays off) instead of trivial
  snowballing.
  - *"As a player, I want a new business to take several turns to earn back its
    cost, so that choosing when and where to build actually matters."*
- **Producer / game designer** — wants a reproducible, evidence-backed balance
  change with a documented lever set and guardrails.
  - *"As a designer, I want the payback curve to scale with card cost and be
    enforced by tests, so future cards stay in band."*
- **Developer** — wants deterministic contracts, before/after metrics, and an
  auditable baseline update.
  - *"As a developer, I want the payback contract and the regenerated baseline
    to be reproducible from a single commit SHA."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Business payback contract (deterministic, no simulation).** A test over
   `src/card-data.csv` computes net payback per income-generating business as
   `cost ÷ (baseIncome − ongoingCost)` and asserts:
   - (a) the mean net payback across income businesses is **4.5–5.5 turns**;
   - (b) payback is **cost-graded**: cheap businesses pay back faster than
     expensive ones (bucket means strictly increasing by cost band, and/or a
     Spearman rank correlation between cost and payback ≥ 0.6);
   - (c) every income business has positive net income
     (`baseIncome > ongoingCost`);
   - (d) intentional exceptions (0-income reputation cards such as the Clinic,
     producer-overridden costs such as the Charity Shop) are explicitly listed
     with rationale.
2. **Compensating parameters tuned and guardrails hold.** After the income
   change, the canonical 200-seed / 60-turn greedy profile satisfies the
   design-intent bands: win-rate ladder `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard`, and
   `avgCoinsPerTurn` / `medianScore` within their bands — **or** the bands are
   consciously revised with documented rationale per the drift workflow.
   Parameter changes stay within balance levers (business `baseIncome` /
   `ongoingCost`, difficulty presets, and — as needed — community-space, event,
   and upgrade costs).
3. **Monte Carlo evidence captured.** Before/after runs across Easy/Medium/Hard
   (greedy; sweep where useful) are recorded with commit SHAs and summarised in
   the work item **and** `docs/main-street/`. The committed baseline
   (`docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`) is regenerated only via the
   **drift-report-then-ask** workflow in
   `docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md` (§0) — never
   silently.
4. **Further-balancing recommendations produced.** A concise artefact (doc or
   work-item comment) presents macro/micro findings (economy health, loss-mode
   decomposition, synergy diversity, outlier/trap cards) and specific,
   prioritised parameter suggestions, each linked to a follow-up work item
   where it is out of scope here.
5. **Documentation updated.** `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md`,
   `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`,
   `docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md`, and any affected
   PRD tables reflect the new payback model and values, including code comments.
6. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (`npm test`).

> Standard criteria also met: at least one testing/validation criterion (AC1),
> documentation updated (AC5), and full suite green (AC6). CHANGELOG.md is
> excluded (managed by the ship pipeline); no CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Constraints

- **Integer ×100 economy** (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6): `card-data.csv` values are
  integer coin-cent units; payback is computed in whole-coin display units and
  incomes must round to integers.
- **Card-data change is a review trigger** (PRD §3.1) → a structured balance
  review with before/after evidence is mandatory.
- **Lever order** (CG-0MSP26Q5N002EH8P): difficulty presets first; card data for
  card-level outliers. Here card income is the explicit target, so card data
  leads and presets compensate.
- **No engine-rule changes** unless justified and separately tracked (e.g. score
  formula, action economy, synergy formula).
- **Preserve deliberate overrides:** incident cards stay free (cost 0);
  community spaces keep their 0-income reputation/synergy role; the Charity Shop
  keeps its producer-set cost; the Clinic keeps its 0-income reputation design;
  hand-held-business ongoing-cost semantics (CG-0MTC31LN3000UHDY) are unchanged.
- **Baseline discipline:** drift is reported and approved before regeneration.
- **Scope-creep guard:** engine changes, new cards, staff/event re-balancing are
  separate work items; record, don't absorb.

## Existing state

- **Card data:** `src/card-data.csv` — 31 businesses, 8 community spaces.
  Business incomes were last raised by CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE
  (`income = old income + 2.4 × ongoingCost`) with `ongoingCost = max(25, cost/4)`,
  producing the current payback profile.
- **Current measured net payback** (whole coins, `cost ÷ (baseIncome − ongoingCost)`):

  | Card | Cost | Income | Ongoing | Net | Net payback |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | Bakery / Diner / Bookshop / Hardware / Boutique | 3.00 | 2.30 | 0.75 | 1.55 | 1.94 |
  | Pawn Shop | 2.00 | 2.30 | 0.75 | 1.55 | 1.29 |
  | Laundromat / Arcade / Food Truck | 4.00 | 2.90 | 1.00 | 1.90 | 2.11 |
  | Barbershop | 5.00 | 4.00 | 1.25 | 2.75 | 1.82 |
  | Cafe | 7.00 | 5.20 | 1.75 | 3.45 | 2.03 |
  | Art Gallery / Day Spa / Private Clinic | 14.00 | 9.40–10.90 | 3.50 | 5.90–7.40 | 1.89–2.37 |
  | Grand Hotel | 16.00 | 12.10 | 4.00 | 8.10 | 1.98 |
  | Charity Shop | 3.00 | 1.50 | 0.75 | 0.75 | 4.00 |
  | Clinic | 9.00 | 0.00 | 0.50 | −0.50 | n/a (rep card) |

  Average net payback ≈ **2.1 turns** over the 30 income businesses.
- **Difficulty presets** (`src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`): Easy 1000 start /
  10000 win threshold / 0.5 synergy; Medium 600 / 12000 / 0.35; Hard 400 /
  15000 / 0.25.
- **Monte Carlo harness:** `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` +
  `src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts` (`npm run monte-carlo`,
  `npm run monte-carlo-sweep`); baseline generator
  `src/scripts/generate-main-street-monte-baseline.ts`; drift report
  `npm run balance:drift-report`.
- **Balance analysis library:** `src/scripts/balance/` (micro M1–M7, macro
  G1–G8, guardrail thresholds, comparison engine); M3
  `computeCostToIncomeRatio` is the static cost-to-income metric.
- **Guardrail tests:** `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts`
  (design intent), `monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` (baseline drift),
  `monte-carlo-balance.test.ts` (smoke).
- **Committed baseline** (`docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`,
  200 seeds / 60 turns): greedy win rate Easy 0.91 / Medium 0.615 / Hard 0.44;
  Medium net liquidity 632.99 (×100 units) and median score 12332.5 (×100).
- **Balancing algorithm/docs:** `src/balance-cards/`,
  `src/scripts/run-balance-cards.ts` (`npm run balance-cards`),
  `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md`.

## Desired change

1. **Derive incomes from a payback target.** Set
   `baseIncome = cost ÷ targetPayback + ongoingCost`, with `targetPayback`
   rising with cost so the **mean across income businesses is ~5 turns** — e.g.
   ~3–4 turns for cost-2–4 cards, ~5 turns for mid-cost (7–10), ~6.5–7 turns
   for cost-14–16 flagships. Round to integer cent units.
2. **Re-tune compensating levers** so the tighter economy stays winnable and
   paced: adjust difficulty presets (starting coins / win thresholds / synergy),
   and review `ongoingCost` and community-space / event / upgrade pricing where
   the payback model breaks down. Document every change and its rationale.
3. **Measure.** Re-run the Monte Carlo harness for each difficulty before and
   after; record metrics and commit SHAs; regenerate the baseline via the drift
   workflow only after review.
4. **Recommend.** Produce further-balancing suggestions from the macro/micro
   reports (e.g. community spaces, events, upgrades, difficulty bands), each
   linked to a follow-up work item.
5. **Enforce.** Add the deterministic payback contract so future card additions
   cannot silently drift out of band.

### Candidate payback targets (illustrative — to be finalised during planning)

| Cost band | Example cards | Target net payback |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2–4 | Pawn Shop, Bakery, Laundromat, Arcade | ~3.5 |
| 5–7 | Barbershop, Cafe, Flower Shop, Teahouse | ~5.0 |
| 8–10 | Yoga Studio, Gym, Physiotherapist, Clinic* | ~5.5 |
| 12–16 | Dentist, Art Gallery, Day Spa, Grand Hotel | ~6.5–7.0 |

\* Clinic has no income by design; excluded from the mean, handled as a
documented exception.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — Re-derive business `baseIncome` (and review
  `ongoingCost`) for the ~5-turn payback target; integer cent units.
- `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — Compensating preset tuning
  (`startingCoins`, `winThreshold`, `synergyBonusPerNeighbor`, incident knobs).
- `tests/main-street/business-payback.test.ts` (new) — Deterministic payback
  contract: mean ≈5, cost-graded monotone, positive net income, documented
  exceptions.
- `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/clinic-health-synergy.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/charity-shop.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/group-a-*`/`expanded-card-pool*`,

- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts`,

  assertions after re-tune.
- `src/scripts/balance/guards/thresholds.ts` — Threshold band updates if the
  review revises them.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/card-metrics.ts` — Extend M3 (or add a companion)

  `src/scripts/generate-main-street-monte-baseline.ts`,
  `src/scripts/balance/drift-report.ts` — Generate before/after evidence.
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — Document the payback model and
  revised per-family strategy.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — Refresh card stat tables.

  spread respects the payback target if the balancing pass is re-run.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE** — Business ongoing costs + income raise
  (`income = old + 2.4 × ongoingCost`); the economy this item re-tunes.
- **CG-0MTC31LN3000UHDY** — Hand-held businesses no longer incur ongoing costs;

- **CG-0MSP26Q5N002EH8P** — Economy re-tune and the "presets first" lever order.

- **CG-0MTH5CC4H003Q4B3** — Investment events cost one action (economy

- **MS-0MUMC6IVF0098WRL** — Per-turn running costs for community spaces.
- **MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M** — Staff cost-reduction effects (interacts with
  effective cost/payback).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Payback definition (assumption).** Net payback = `cost ÷ (baseIncome −
  ongoingCost)` in whole coins, excluding synergy/event income. "Profit" is read
  as revenue minus running cost. Gross `cost ÷ baseIncome` is also reported.
  *Producer confirmation requested (see Appendix Q1).*
- **Magnitude.** Reaching ~5 turns means roughly a **2.4× income cut** (or
  equivalent), which will materially tighten the economy: expect lower liquidity,
  slower score growth, and more bankruptcies. Compensating levers must be tuned
  together, not income alone.
- **Synergy distortion.** Low base incomes make synergy/`{SYNERGY_RATE}` a larger
  share of a business's income, potentially making placement dominate base
  economy. Monitor synergy utilisation and diversity in the macro report.
- **Community spaces, events, upgrades.** These carry no business payback; if
  their pricing is left untouched they may become relatively over/under-valued.
  Review is in scope for AC2/AC4 but changes are evidence-led.
- **Guardrail churn.** A large intentional balance change will breach
  baseline-relative drift. Follow the drift-report-then-ask workflow and do not
  silently regenerate.
- **Scope-creep risk.** New cards, staff re-balancing, and engine-rule changes
  are out of scope; record as linked follow-up work items (AC4).
- **Determinism.** The payback contract must be fully deterministic (CSV-only),
  independent of simulation seeds.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

All entries below are research-driven and are recorded for producer
confirmation; the recommended interpretation was used to draft this brief.

- **Q1 (payback definition):** *Should the 5-turn payback be measured net of the
  business's per-turn running cost (`cost ÷ (baseIncome − ongoingCost)`) or
  gross (`cost ÷ baseIncome`)?*
  **Answer (recommended, pending producer confirmation):** Net of running cost —
  "turns to profit" is read as recovering the purchase cost after operating
  costs, which is the game's actual economic break-even. Gross payback will also
  be reported for transparency. Research: `ongoingCost = max(25, cost/4)` is
  deducted every turn (`applyBusinessOngoingCosts`, business-ongoing-cost
  tests); M3 currently models only gross `cost/baseIncome`, so a net companion
  is proposed. Source: `src/card-data.csv`, `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`,
  `docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md`.
- **Q2 (average weighting & spread):** *Is the "average of 5 turns" a simple
  mean across income businesses, and how should it vary with cost?*
  **Answer (recommended, pending producer confirmation):** A simple mean of ~5
  turns across income-generating businesses, with a cost-graded spread (cheap
  ≈3.5, mid ≈5, flagship ≈6.5–7), exactly as the operator described ("more
  expensive … longer … cheaper … quicker"). Clinic (0 income) and Charity Shop
  (manual override) are documented exceptions. Source: operator request; current
  payback table (this brief).
- **Q3 (compensating levers):** *Which parameters may be adjusted to keep the
  game winnable?*
  **Answer (recommended, pending producer confirmation):** Balance levers only —
  difficulty presets, business `ongoingCost`, and community-space/event/upgrade
  pricing as needed. Engine rules (score formula, action economy) are out of
  scope and would be raised as separate work items. Research: the "presets
  first, card data for outliers" lever order in
  `docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md` §4. Source: repo docs.
- **Q4 (guardrail bands):** *If the tighter economy moves guardrail metrics
  outside the current bands, revise bands or keep tuning?*
  **Answer (recommended, pending producer confirmation):** Tune the compensating
  levers first; revise a band only if the measured outcome is genuinely the

`https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-main-street/`.

**Reuse.** Mirror `core/.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (same action versions,
`pages` concurrency group, `github-pages` environment, three-step configure /
upload / deploy) but drop the sibling-game composition step: this repo's
`./configs/game.json` preset already selects the core-owned Gym plus Main Street.

**Test-first.** The workflow contract test is written before the workflow file and
committed with it, so this item lands green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **1.** Auto-deploy on ship: every push to `main` runs a GitHub Actions workflow that builds `tce-main-street` and deploys `dist/` to GitHub Pages at `https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-main-street/`.
- **2.** Gated deployment: the workflow runs unit tests and the production build first, and a failing test or build blocks deployment so no artefact is published.
- **3.** No stored SSH credentials: the build composes the `./core` submodule from the public core repo over HTTPS, needing no SSH secrets or `ssh-key` input.
- **4.** Main Street only (with launcher): the published site shows the launcher with exactly one playable example game, Main Street.
- **5.** The build uses the single-game preset and never `GAMES_CONFIG=full`, and no sibling `tce-<game>` repository is cloned, so no other example game can appear in the selector; the core-owned Gym is always present.
- **6.** Steps are ordered install (`npm ci`) → test (`npm test`) → build (`npm run build`) → `actions/configure-pages@v5` → `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3` (`path: dist`) → `actions/deploy-pages@v4`, and no other trigger can publish unreleased work.
- **7.** `permissions` are exactly `contents: read`, `pages: write`, `id-token: write`; `concurrency` is `group: pages` with `cancel-in-progress: true`; the job uses `environment: github-pages` and exposes the deployed `page_url`.
- **8.** `tests/deploy/deploy-workflow.test.ts` parses the workflow YAML and asserts the trigger, step order, permissions, concurrency, the absence of secret/SSH references, and the absence of `GAMES_CONFIG=full`; the test fails if any of those are removed.
- **9.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes: `npm test` is green.

- Add `tests/deploy/deploy-workflow.test.ts` first (adapted from `core/tests/scripts/deploy-workflow.test.ts`).
